title: Latency & Error Budget Cost Tradeoffs — 90-day Sprint Proposal
body:
Executive summary:
This 90-day sprint proposal frames a cross-functional program to reconcile latency SLOs and error-budget practices with platform cost targets for model serving. Goal: define measurable tradeoffs, run a sequence of controlled experiments, and deliver an operational decision guide that lets product teams select latency vs. cost profiles with predictable error-budget outcomes.

Why this matters now:
- Rising demand for low-latency chat endpoints is increasing tail-latency incidents and burst capacity spend.
- Platform teams have ad-hoc overrides (larger batch sizes, aggressive autoscaling) that reduce immediate cost but increase customer-facing latency spikes and error-budget burns.
- We need a repeatable roadmap so product owners can choose service profiles without surprise budget or reliability regressions.

Scope (in):
- Model-serving infra (hosted API and Dedicated pools) latency SLOs for inference endpoints (p50, p95, p99)
- Error budget definition and burn accounting per service route
- Cost model linking autoscaler behavior, batching, and KV cache hit rate to per-token/per-request unit cost
- Cross-team experiment design (serving-runtime, infra autoscaler, SRE, product-hosted-api)

Out of scope (for this 90d):
- Full private-deployment compliance work
- Long-term kernel selection changes beyond experiment flags

Primary objectives (90d):
1) Produce a clear mapping: Delta latency (p95) <-> Expected error-budget burn rate <-> $/1000 requests impact (within ±15% accuracy).
2) Run 3 production-canary experiments to validate cost/latency tradeoffs and update autoscaler and batching defaults.
3) Publish an operational decision guide and a dashboard template for product owners.
4) Create rollback-safe rollout gates and runbooks.

Key stakeholders:
- Platform Engineering (owner): Avery Chen (project lead), Marcus Li (autoscaler), Priya Nair (cost modeling)
- Serving Runtime: Diego Morales (runtime experiments), Lina Park (KV cache)
- SRE: Pager rotations & runbook owners
- Product (hosted-api): Feature owners for top 10 routes by traffic
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: communicate changes affecting Dedicated customers

Success metrics (measurable):
- Accuracy: Cost-latency mapping validated to within ±15% of predicted values for at least 2 of the 3 canary routes.
- Stability: No P0 incidents attributable to experiments during canaries (30-day post-canary watch)
- Adoption: At least 3 product routes adopt the decision guide profiles by sprint end
- Observability: Dashboard with per-route SLO, error-budget, cost-rate, and autoscaler decisions live in Console.

SLO definitions (candidate):
- Route A (interactive chat): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms, error rate < 0.2%
- Route B (batch embeddings): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5%
- Route C (reranking): p50 < 100ms, p95 < 260ms, error rate < 0.3%
Note: these are draft and will be tuned after baseline measurement.

Cost modeling approach:
- Unit cost = infra_cost_per_minute * (GPU_fraction_allocated_for_route) / (requests_served_per_minute)
- Inputs: GPU spot vs. on-demand price, average request length (tokens), KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency (tokens/request), autoscaler cooldowns
- Deliverable: a parameterized notebook that takes route inputs and outputs expected $/1000 requests across configuration vectors.

Experiment slate (canaries):
- Canary 1 (batching vs. latency): Increase batch-size target by +30% on low-concurrency worker pool for Route B; measure p95 and cost. Acceptance: shows >=12% cost reduction without >10% increase in p95 errors.
- Canary 2 (autoscaler smoothing): Increase autoscaler cooldown from 60s -> 120s for Route A traffic class; monitor tail-latency and error-budget burn under a scheduled traffic ramp. Acceptance: stable error rate with measurable reduction in transient GPU spin-ups and cost.
- Canary 3 (cache-first): KV cache TTL tuned from 5s->30s for common prompt prefixes on Route C; measure KV hit rate, p95, and downstream compute savings. Acceptance: KV hit rate increase >20% and cost reduction commensurate with model-serving time saved, latency unchanged.

Measurement & dashboards:
- Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, request queue depth, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, autoscaler scale events, cost per minute per pool.
- Example query snippets (Prometheus):
  - p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
  - error rate: sum(rate(inference_errors_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) by (route)
  - autoscaler churn: increase(autoscaler_scale_events_total[5m])
- Dashboard: one-page per route showing SLO, error-budget remaining, cost velocity, and recent autoscaler events.

Runbooks & rollout gates:
- Canary gating: 1) safety window (low traffic hours), 2) watchers assigned from SRE, 3) automatic revert if p95 increases >15% or error rate doubles in 10m window.
- Rollback steps: revert feature flag -> scale pools to baseline config -> escalate to oncall leads.

Cross-functional cadence (recommended):
- Weekly experiment sync (Mon 11:00) — platform, runtime, SRE, product reps
- Bi-weekly steering (Tue 15:00) — exec-level check-ins and signoff for production canaries
- Daily watch during active canaries (Slack huddles + standup minutes)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Canary traffic not representative -> Mitigate: synthetic ramping with traffic replay + real user sampling.
- Risk: Cost model underestimates tail resource usage -> Mitigate: include 95th percentile utilization in model inputs and run sensitivity analysis.
- Risk: Dedicated customers impacted by default changes -> Mitigate: isolate changes behind flags, coordinate with Solutions Eng and offer per-customer opt-outs.

Dependencies & blockers:
- Accurate tagging of routes in telemetry (ticket: JIRA-TELEM-77)
- Runtime feature flags for batching and cache TTL (PR: serving-runtime #1287)
- Cost data export access to finance for per-pool pricing (Confluence doc pinned above)

Decision artifacts to deliver by Q2 checkpoint:
- Parameterized cost-latency notebook (notebook URL to be published)
- Three canary experiment writeups (outcomes, graphs, decisions)
- Operational decision guide: 3 recommended profiles (latency-first, cost-balanced, cost-min) with guardrails and runbook steps
- Dashboard template and pre-configured alert rules in Console

Near-term (first 30 days) sprint plan:
- Week 1: baseline data collection (all signals), align product owners for top 10 routes, finalize SLO drafts
- Week 2: complete cost model inputs, finish telemetry tagging fixes, create experiment playbooks
- Week 3: small-scale lab tests in staging for batching and cache tweaks; implement feature flags
- Week 4: begin Canary 1 during low-traffic window with SRE watchers

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff):
- What is the acceptable monthly cost delta threshold for product teams when selecting "cost-balanced" profile? (Finance input required)
- Should Dedicated customers have separate default profiles or always be opted into customer-managed profiles?
- How long should we wait before marking a canary as successful (30d watch vs. 14d)?

Next steps (owner names included):
- Avery Chen: schedule weekly sync and create experiment tracking board (JIRA-RELIAB-402)
- Priya Nair + Finance: finalize per-pool cost export by Jan 22
- Diego Morales: implement runtime feature flags for batching TTL and autoscaler knobs by Jan 29
- Lina Park: produce KV-cache telemetry baseline by Jan 25

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally constrained to a 90d operational program rather than a long-term architecture change. Focus feedback on the experiment slate, acceptance criteria, and what product owners need to adopt recommended profiles.

Appendix (quick links & refs):
- Ops cost framework (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/REL/ops-cost-framework
